belief.answer: Put N=binom(n,2), H=(n^(n−2))!, B=2^(N+n), and δ(x)=⌊1/(|x|+1)⌋. For 0≤b<2^N, let A_b be the symmetric zero-diagonal matrix whose upper-triangular entries, in lexicographic order, are the binary digits of b, least significant first. Set d_{b,i}=∑_j(A_b)_{ij}, L_b=diag(d_{b,1},…,d_{b,n})−A_b, a_b=det L_b^{[{n}]}, f_{b,uv}=det L_b^{[{u,v}]}, q_b=a_b+δ(a_b), and w_b=(1−δ(a_b))∏_{i=2}^n δ(d_{b,i}−d_{b,1}), where L^{[S]} deletes rows and columns indexed by S. Then the following uniform explicit exact formula holds throughout the requested domain: \boxed{t_n=\frac1H\left\lfloor\log_B\!\left(1+\sum_{b=0}^{2^N-1}w_b\sum_{1\le u<v\le n}B^{Hn d_{b,1}f_{b,uv}/q_b}\right)\right\rfloor}.
